page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is a dedicated instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The server features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Storage is bundled as a 5760 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong computational capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance placing in the top 25%. Passmark CPU and physics tests also rank in the top 25%, reflecting solid raw processing power. While memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is average, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth are top-tier, placing in the top 10% at 467.73 GB/sec and 282.99 GB/sec respectively. Other metrics, such as Redis SET operations at 51.19 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 20.63 GB/sec, fall within average ranges.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high resource density, combining a substantial memory footprint with a very large local NVMe storage allocation. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without noisy-neighbor issues. However, a potential tradeoff is the lack of specialized hardware accelerators like GPUs or advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, which may limit its efficiency for deep learning or highly specialized cryptographic workloads.

This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. Appropriate use cases include hosting large relational or non-relational databases, executing data-dense ETL pipelines, running memory-cached web applications, and handling general-purpose enterprise workloads that require high local storage capacity and consistent CPU performance.
description: The Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 24 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs, 192.0 GB of RAM, and a 5760 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this server delivers strong CPU performance, with stress-ng and Passmark benchmarks placing it in the top 25%. It also exhibits top-tier large-block memory bandwidth, reaching 467.73 GB/sec for reads and 282.99 GB/sec for writes. While it lacks GPU acceleration and AVX-512 support, its high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core and massive local storage make it highly resource-dense. This configuration is optimal for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, and enterprise application hosting.
